=== Fy26 annual report ===
*Sample organization. Fernwood Tool Library, Alder Falls, and every person named here are fictional.*
Fiscal year July 1, 2025 to June 30, 2026. Prepared by the staff for members, partners and the board.

Fernwood Tool Library lends tools the way a public library lends books. Members borrow drills, ladders, tile saws,
carpet cleaners, pressure washers, sewing machines and garden tools for a week at a time, and bring them back for the
next neighbor. We opened in a rented storefront at 418 Wren Street in Alder Falls in 2019. Membership runs on a
sliding scale from $0 to $60 a year; about one member in four pays nothing.
We have one full-time director, one part-time shop lead, and 46 volunteers. The storefront is open 22 hours a week:
Wednesday and Friday afternoons and Sunday.

- **Members.** 1,962 active members on June 30, 2026, up from 1,410 a year earlier.

response.draft:
Slide 1: Open When Our Neighbors Can Come
Fernwood Tool Library, Alder Falls
A proposal to the Alder Falls Community Fund
Request: $46,500 a year for two years ($93,000 in all)
To add evenings and Saturdays: 34 open hours a week instead of 22
Sample organization: Fernwood Tool Library, Alder Falls, and all people named are fictional

Slide 2: What Members Told Us
512 members answered our May 2026 survey
We asked what keeps them from borrowing more
47% named our hours, far ahead of any other answer
Next answers: "the tool I wanted was out" (19%), parking (11%)
Many work weekday afternoons and can't reach us before we close at 6 p.m.
"I've walked past at 6:15 more times than I can count. The lights are on and the door is locked."

Slide 3: The People We're Missing: Millbrook
Millbrook has 22% of Alder Falls renters
Only 9% of our members live there
61% of Millbrook members who answered named our hours, the highest of any neighborhood
Most of them work shifts
Our current hours leave out the neighbors who could use us most

Slide 4: The Door Is the Limit, Not the Tools
344 hold requests were waiting on June 30, 2026
Most were for the tile saw, carpet cleaner and pressure washer
Holds wait an average of 11 days
On the 3 days we're open, a returned tool often goes back out within the hour
On the 4 days we're closed, it sits on the shelf

Slide 5: What We Already Deliver (FY2026)
1,962 active members, up from 1,410
9,840 tool loans, up from 7,215
2,350 tools on the shelves; only 4% of loans came back late
14 repair cafes: 438 of 611 items fixed
46 volunteers gave 3,120 hours
Sliding-scale membership, $0 to $60; about 1 in 4 members pays nothing
Members estimate the library saved them a median of $180 over the year

Slide 6: What the Grant Pays For
A part-time coordinator, 25 hours a week
A trained lead on hand whenever power tools go out; volunteers can't cover every new shift
New hours:
Tuesday and Thursday evenings until 8 p.m.
Saturday, 9 a.m. to 3 p.m.
Open 34 hours a week instead of 22

Slide 7: The Money
FY2026 budget: $212,400, closed even, no debt
Added cost of longer hours: $46,500 a year (coordinator, plus utilities and supplies)
FY2027 budget before the board: $258,900
Request: $46,500 a year for two years, $93,000 in all
Today each loan costs about $21.60
A new tile saw costs about $400; a weekend store rental about $65

Slide 8: What We Expect, and How We'll Report It
Our estimate: about 2,500 more loans a year once members learn the new times
This is a staff estimate, not a promise
We will report actual results to the Fund, including:
Loans on the new evening and Saturday shifts
Hold wait times
Membership growth in Millbrook

Slide 9: Thank You
Members asked us to open the door when they can come
With the Fund's help, we can
Rosa Delacroix-Imari, Director (Sample)
Fernwood Tool Library, 418 Wren Street, Alder Falls
